2026-12-21.title: Monday after the Sunday before Yaldo
readings: Your faith is proclaimed throughout the world
In him was life, and the life was light
2026-12-21.alt: Season of Yaldo and Denho. The last days of the Twenty-Five Days' Fast.
2026-12-21.verse: All things came into being through him, and without him not one thing came into being. What has come into being in him was life, and the life was the light of all people.
theo: Paul begins his letter to the Romans with thanksgiving: “your faith is proclaimed throughout the world.” He longs to visit them, not only to give but to receive: “so that we may be mutually encouraged by each other's faith, both yours and mine.” He feels himself a debtor to everyone, Greeks and barbarians, wise and foolish. Faith is never private property; it is a gift we owe to others.

In these last days before Yaldo the Church reads the prologue of John slowly, a few verses each day. Today: “All things came into being through him… What has come into being in him was life, and the life was the light of all people.” The child of Bethlehem is the one through whom the stars and the shepherds and the ox and the ass were made. The Creator enters his own creation as a creature.
outline: Whose faith has encouraged you this year?
A gift to share with the world.
“The life was the light of all people.”
live: Send a Christmas message that speaks of Jesus, not only of the holidays.

2026-12-21.prayer: Eternal Word, through whom all things were made, you come to us as light and life. Let our faith encourage others, and let us welcome you with wonder at your coming. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbono the eternal Word, through whom all things were made, comes to us. We share in his life and light.

quick: Faith is a gift we owe to others.

2026-12-21.question: Whose faith can I encourage this Christmas?

family.explain: Jesus was with God before the world began. He made everything, and he is the light no darkness can put out.
family.intention: We pray for those who live far from home and need encouragement.
family.ask: Ask: “Whom can we encourage in their faith this week?”

pm.open: Eternal Word of the Father, light of all people, as we gather, let us be encouraged by one another's faith and share your light. Amen.
share: Paul says we are mutually encouraged by each other's faith (Romans 1:12). Whose faith encourages me?
Paul says: I am a debtor (Romans 1:14). To whom do I owe the Gospel?
How does it change my view of Yaldo to know the Child is the eternal Word?
pm.resp: Christ our light, shine upon us.
interc: For the Church, that her faith may be proclaimed throughout the world.
For young people studying and working far from home.
For those whose faith is weak, that they may be encouraged.
For all who live in darkness, that the light may reach them.
For our group, that we may encourage one another.
pm.close: Lord God, your Word was in the beginning with you. Fill us with his life and light, and make us encourage one another in faith as we await his birth. Amen.

illus: Every Yaldo week, an elderly couple in Kayamkulam writes short letters of encouragement to the young people of their parish who are studying or working away from home. Many of those young people keep the letters for years.

homily: Dear friends, St Paul begins his letter to the Romans with thanksgiving: I thank my God through Jesus Christ for all of you, because your faith is proclaimed throughout the world (Romans 1:8). He longs to see them, so that we may be mutually encouraged by each other's faith (Romans 1:12).

Faith is not a private possession; it grows through sharing. When we pray together, visit each other and speak about God, we encourage one another. Paul, the great apostle, also needed the encouragement of ordinary believers.

Paul says: I am a debtor both to Greeks and to barbarians, both to the wise and to the foolish (Romans 1:14). He felt he owed the Gospel to everyone. We too are debtors: we received the faith freely, and we owe it to others.

The Gospel today is the prologue of John: in the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. In him was life, and the life was the light of all people (John 1:1–4). Four days before Yaldo, the Church lifts our eyes from the manger to eternity.

The Child we will adore is the eternal Word. Through him all things were made, including you and me. When we hold the image of the Child in our homes, we are looking at the Creator who became a creature out of love.
In these last days, let us encourage someone in their faith: a phone call, a visit, a word of hope. And let us repay our debt by sharing the light we have received. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus made everything: the sun, the stars and you! Say thank you to Jesus for everything He made.
